issues.description: Typo 'stlib's' in the .. deprecated:: 4.3 directive should be 'stdlib's'.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged this. The Sphinx directive contains a typo that will render in published docs. Trivial one-character fix in the same commit.

issues.description: Deprecation message does not give callers the exact replacement recipe.
issues.detail: The warning names contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr but never shows how to compose them when both streams are redirected at once. Add one clause pointing users to nested with-statements or ExitStack so the substitution is unambiguous.

issues.description: Deprecation test matches only a loose suffix of the warning message.
issues.detail: The pytest.warns match pattern keys on the 'Please use...' tail, so any reword of the prefix passes silently, and the invariant that redirection still works for stderr and on the exception path is unstated. Match on something stable and add a stderr / exception-restore case.

synthesis.summary: Consensus: ACCEPT with trivial fixup. The panel agrees this is a small, well-scoped, single-purpose deprecation that correctly defers to stdlib contextlib helpers and leaves the original generator's control flow untouched under the @deprecated wrapper. The diff is readable, matches surrounding style, and includes a news fragment plus a test that exercises the warning. Three P2 nits worth fixing in passing: a 'stlib' typo in the Sphinx directive, an incomplete replacement recipe for the both-streams case, and a loose warning-match in the test. None block merge.
